_metadata.validated_against: README.md — QuizLive Cloud (Academic Enterprise Edition, refactored 2026-06-04)

discrepancies.resolution: README is the authoritative documentation source for this repository. Version is recorded as 4.18. If the deployed environment runs 4.19.x, update the README badge and this file to reflect the actual installed version to maintain a single source of truth.

discrepancies.readme_value: Single instance: pm2 start src/app.js --name quizlive-api
discrepancies.resolution: The README Quick Start and Phase 9.6 both reference single-instance PM2 start commands. Cluster mode via ecosystem.config.js is referenced in infrastructure/pm2/ecosystem.config.js. In a 1-vCPU, 1024 MB VM (quizlivemedium), cluster mode with instances=max resolves to a single worker process and provides no throughput benefit. Single-instance mode is recommended for this deployment profile.

discrepancies.readme_value: Local development server on Windows workstation (npm run dev, http://localhost:5173)
discrepancies.resolution: The README describes local execution of the Vite dev server as the primary deployment model for the academic demonstration environment. Vercel is listed in the source JSON as a suggested future platform. Both deployment models are documented here — local for demonstration, Vercel for production. The mixed-content HTTPS/HTTP constraint applies to Vercel deployments and is documented in the frontend_deployment section below.

project.name: QuizLive
project.full_title: QuizLive Cloud — Private Cloud IaaS Based on Apache CloudStack and KVM for a Real-Time Interactive Quiz Platform
project.context: University capstone project for the Cloud Computing course. Implements a full private cloud IaaS stack using Apache CloudStack and KVM, hosting a real-time quiz application built with React, Express, and Socket.IO.

academic_context.department: Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Universitas Indonesia

repository_modules.name: Infrastructure Artifacts
repository_modules.description: Backup copies of CloudStack host, NFS, Netplan, and PM2 configuration files extracted from the Ubuntu Server deployment environment.

cloudstack_version.validation_note: See DISC-001. Reconcile version across README badge, this file, and the actual installed packages to maintain a single source of truth.

virtualization_host.layer: VirtualBox (nested virtualization — hardware-assisted KVM within a VirtualBox guest)

bridge_interface.name: cloudbr0
bridge_interface.description: Linux bridge interface that serves as the unified network fabric for CloudStack management, KVM agent communication, and all guest VM traffic on the physical LAN.

public_ip_pool.description: CloudStack allocates addresses from this pool for Virtual Router public interfaces and any Elastic IP assignments within the zone.

system_vm_template.description: Pre-built System VM template deployed to secondary storage during zone initialization. Required for automated provisioning of SSVM and CPVM.

reserved_ip_range.description: IP addresses reserved for CloudStack System VMs within the pod. Must not overlap with DHCP-assigned or statically configured host addresses.

host.security_note: Root SSH access is enabled to satisfy CloudStack's default host registration requirements. In production environments, this should be restricted to the management network or replaced with key-based authentication.

physical_lan.description: Physical campus LAN. The Windows workstation accesses the CloudStack management dashboard and Virtual Router public IP through this network segment.

cloudstack_public_ip_pool.description: CloudStack public IP address pool. The Virtual Router acquires 192.168.101.232 from this pool as its Source NAT public interface.

isolated_guest_network.name: QuizLive-Isolated-OK
isolated_guest_network.description: Isolated CloudStack guest network. Guest VMs reside in this subnet and are not directly reachable from the physical LAN. All inbound access is mediated by the Virtual Router via DNAT port forwarding.

firewall_ingress_rules.purpose: SSH administrative access to guest VM via DNAT
QuizLive API (HTTP REST + Socket.IO WebSocket) access

port_forwarding_rules.purpose: SSH to quizlive-db-vm via Virtual Router public IP
port_forwarding_rules.rationale: TCP port 22 on the shared public IP 192.168.101.232 would conflict with the CloudStack host's SSH service. Mapping guest VM SSH to alternate port 2222 eliminates this conflict and allows independent SSH sessions to both the host (192.168.101.220:22) and the guest VM (192.168.101.232:2222).

port_forwarding_rules.purpose: Expose Node.js Express REST API and Socket.IO WebSocket endpoint to external clients

nfs.server_description: CloudStack hypervisor host (Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS) acting as NFS server

exports.description: Active VM disk volumes (QCOW2 images). Hosts all running and stopped VM disk images managed by CloudStack.
System VM templates, ISO images, and VM snapshots. The no_root_squash option is required for CloudStack's storage management operations executed as root.

cloudstack_image.name: Ubuntu-22.04-Server
cloudstack_image.description: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS Server — used as the guest VM operating system installation medium

local_serving_procedure.step_1: Download ISO on Windows workstation: ubuntu-22.04.5-live-server-amd64.iso
local_serving_procedure.step_2: Transfer to CloudStack host: scp ubuntu-22.04.5-live-server-amd64.iso ubuntu@192.168.101.220:~/iso/
local_serving_procedure.step_3: Serve via Python HTTP server: cd ~/iso && python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 192.168.101.220
local_serving_procedure.rationale: LAN-local ISO serving eliminates SSVM download timeout failures caused by internet bandwidth constraints and intermittent DNS instability in the lab environment.

compute_offerings.name: quizlivesmall
compute_offerings.display_text: Optimal for lightweight stateless services: API gateway, load balancer, bastion host, and microservices. 1 vCPU, 512 MB RAM, 10 GB local SSD storage. Designed for high-density deployment with thin provisioning.
compute_offerings.intended_workload: Stateless API gateway, load balancer, bastion host, microservices
compute_offerings.deployment_note: Originally designated for a dedicated API gateway VM. Not used in the current deployment; the application and database are consolidated on a single quizlivemedium VM to maintain stability under the nested virtualization resource constraints.

compute_offerings.name: quizlivemedium
compute_offerings.display_text: Dedicated for relational database workloads (MySQL 8.0). Balanced compute resources: 1 vCPU, 1024 MB RAM, 20 GB local SSD storage. Supports transactional integrity and moderate concurrency. Thin provisioning enabled for efficient storage usage.
compute_offerings.intended_workload: MySQL 8.0 relational database, Node.js application server, transactional processing, moderate concurrency

initial_console_access.method: CloudStack VNC Console (View Console in dashboard)
initial_console_access.reason: Guest VM resides in a non-routable isolated network (10.1.1.0/24). Direct SSH from the physical LAN is not possible prior to port forwarding configuration.

public_service_endpoints.service: QuizLive REST API and Socket.IO WebSocket

host_based_firewall.role: Defense-in-depth layer. Provides host-level access control independent of the CloudStack Virtual Router perimeter firewall.

application_user.privilege_principle: Principle of least privilege — remote access is restricted to DML operations; DDL grants are localhost-only for schema migrations.

cluster_mode.validation_note: See DISC-002. On a 1-vCPU VM, instances=max resolves to a single worker process. Single-instance start command is equivalent and recommended for this deployment profile.

environment_variables.security_note: Credentials and secrets must not be committed to the repository. The .env file is listed in .gitignore. The agent.properties template file (infrastructure/cloudstack/agent.properties.template) may also contain sensitive values and should be reviewed before any public repository push.

required_keys.description: Base URL for REST API requests to the CloudStack-hosted backend
WebSocket server URL for Socket.IO real-time event connection

local_development.description: Primary deployment model for the academic demonstration environment. Frontend serves over HTTP, connecting to the backend via the Virtual Router public IP.

production_build.description: Generates optimized static assets for production hosting.

cloud_hosting.validation_note: See DISC-003. Vercel (or any HTTPS-hosted platform) requires the backend to also be accessible via HTTPS to satisfy browser Mixed Content policy. Recommended solutions: Cloudflare Tunnel, Ngrok, or a reverse proxy with TLS termination placed in front of 192.168.101.232:3000.

mixed_content_resolution.problem: Browser Mixed Content policy blocks HTTP API/WebSocket requests from HTTPS-served pages.

solutions.applicable_when: Public HTTPS access without modifying network or firewall rules
Temporary HTTPS tunneling for testing or demonstration

disabled_configurations.disabled_reason: Cloud-init's default DHCP assignment on enp0s3 is suppressed to prevent address conflicts with the statically configured cloudbr0 bridge.

VirtualBox NAT interface configuration is intentionally unused. Outbound internet connectivity for both the CloudStack host and guest VMs is provided through the cloudbr0 bridge routed via the physical campus gateway, eliminating conflicting routing table entries.

critical_setting.description: The agent must bind to the cloudbr0 bridge IP. Binding to the NAT interface or localhost prevents the management server from establishing the control-plane connection required for VM lifecycle operations.

cloudstack_agent.security_note: The agent.properties file may contain sensitive authentication passphrases. Review for secrets before committing to any public repository.

end_to_end_request_flow.description: Full request path from client browser to application database and back
